answer: Each agent ID earns voting weight only through peer vouching, and every voucher gives up part of its own reputation score, which it loses if the vouchee is later flagged. We call that score jade. A raven auditor samples vouch graphs every week and looks for dense clusters that connect to the honest graph through only a few edges. A farm can't recycle one patron's jade across fifty fakes, since each vouch drains that patron's balance. Every extra fake therefore needs fresh jade from an honest agent who will take the risk, and the harbor of trusted IDs shrinks as more of them get burned.
